name: George Kittle

background.fact: Born October 9, 1993 in Madison, Wisconsin, moved to Iowa in 2000, and attended high school in Iowa City, Cedar Falls and Norman, Oklahoma. The data file lists Norman, OK as his birthplace; Wikipedia says Madison, so the two disagree.
background.confidence: from Wikipedia; data file differs on birthplace

background.fact: He played at Iowa from 2012 to 2016 under Kirk Ferentz, finishing with 48 receptions for 737 yards and 10 touchdowns, and the 49ers took him in the fifth round of the 2017 draft (pick 146).
background.confidence: from Wikipedia (draft slot also in research/data/PYT-TE.json)

background.fact: He is a seven-time Pro Bowler and was a first-team All-Pro in 2019 and 2023.
Listed at 6 ft 4 in, 250 lb, jersey 85, age 33, in his 10th NFL season, all with San Francisco. Combine: 4.52 forty, 35 inch vertical, 132 inch broad jump.
Career regular season totals through 132 games: 633 catches, 8,491 yards, 57 touchdowns; fantasy average 9.03 points a game under league scoring.

family.fact: His father, Bruce, was a four-year letterman and co-captain of Iowa's 1982 Rose Bowl team and later a college coach; his mother, Jan Krieger, is in the Iowa Girls' High School Athletic Union Hall of Fame and was an All-America basketball player at Drake.
He married Claire Till, whom he met at Iowa where she played basketball, on April 9, 2019. His older sister Emma is married to Cody Ponce.

He and Claire launched a charity called the Kittle fund aimed at strengthening the community, and visited a children's hospital in connection with an Iowa game. Headlines only; the articles were not read.

outlook_next_game.lean: plays with heavy target volume; expected around 9 to 14 fantasy points with a touchdown upside
reasons: He is active and healthy, with 7 or more targets in three straight games and a 23.2 percent target share, and Evans is likely out again.
San Francisco has a 29.5 implied total in a 55.5 total game, and Dallas allows the fourth-highest tight end catch rate.
His 2026 road average is only 3.47 points with no road touchdowns, and the last two games produced 6.8 and 5.8 points, so the floor is low.
Past Dallas games were strong when he scored (24.7 in 2023, 18.8 in 2024), and Dallas is without Ferguson but has Caleb Downs to cover him.

scouts_read: Kittle is healthy and should play most of the game, so the question is touchdowns, not volume. He has seen seven or more targets three games in a row, leads the team in targets, and Mike Evans looks set to miss a third straight game. Dallas allows a high catch rate to tight ends, and San Francisco has a team total near 29.5, which supports a good day. The concern is that his road games this season have produced almost nothing (3.47 points a game, no touchdowns) and his last two games were under 7 points despite heavy targets. I would project about 11 points, with a catch or two near the goal line deciding whether it reaches 18 or more.
